title: 建築デザイン総合演習Ｂ
subtitle: Architectural Integrated Exercises for Design B
teachers:
TANISHIGE Yoshiyuki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: This class is the final stage of the architectural design exercise. Understand the function and composition of large public buildings or complex urban spaces, and plan and design them. In particular, at the stage just before Project Design Ⅲ, the goal is to develop a variety of conditions and functions, and to develop creative abilities that can be integrated as plans and design proposals.
advice:
Assignment is design and planning of buildings and cities with special surrounding environment and complicated required functions. The design issues are roughly divided into three issues (see below).
However, in addition to general design drawings, students propose appropriate and attractive expressions using drawings and sentences showing concepts, model photographs, CG, etc.
1) A large-scale building that satisfies the various functions of facilities, such as elementary school buildings and multicultural buildings in central Kanazawa, and that requires attractive architectural spaces. (two assignments).
2) Planning issues for integrated urban design of buildings and external spaces by decoding and re-editing the contexts of cities and towns (two assignments).
3) Renovation of buildings with changing the use of existing public buildings (one asignment).
４）The task of designing the roof of the plaza while learning techniques such as optimization using visual programming (one asignment).

For the first task, you can freely choose one of the four tasks (1), (2), and (3), and for the second task, you can freely choose one from the four options (1), (2), and (4), and create your work.
requiredKnowledge:
This course is based on basic knowledge of architecture in general and the design ability of architectural design I and II, Architectural Integrated Exercises for Design A.
Students try to apply the knowledge related to the planning and design of architecture and exterior space learned in various classes to the design work.
If you choose Course D in ④ above and have not completed the credits for "Architectural Information Design" in the previous semester, you will need to study visual programming (Rhino+Grasshopper) in advance.

activityGoals.body: Students can analyze the characteristics of the urban area, traditional space, natural environment of location.
Students can develop their ability to organize and design various spaces as architecture and urban space.
Students can analyze the characteristics of the local culture and community and reflect them in urban design.
Students can understand and propose about conversion of existing architecture by renovation project.
Students can work on three-dimensional shape optimization of architectural forms using visual programming.
Students can create and express drawings, models, photographs, and texts as works, and presentate beautifully.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Satisfy the function of large-scale architecture sufficiently and have a good architectural plan and design. (2) A comfortable urban design that satisfies the urban functions has been proposed. (3) The architectural use change is properly planned and designed. (4)Design proposals are made through optimization of architectural forms.Of the above 4goals, the goals according to student's own task selection have been achieved. Furthermore, they have deepened these as more original and attractive contents, and have proposed using advanced and beautiful presentations.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Satisfy the function of large-scale architecture sufficiently and have a good architectural plan and design. (2) A comfortable urban design that satisfies the urban functions has been proposed. (3) The architectural use change is properly planned and designed. (4)Design proposals are made through optimization of architectural forms.Of the above 4 goals, the goals according to student's own task selection have been achieved. Further, these contents can be properly described as drawings.
